verdict.rationale: Jina Reader documents a prebuilt container image of its open-source branch on GitHub Container Registry, bundling headless Chrome, LibreOffice and CJK fonts. It also supports pointing a self-run instance at an S3-compatible cache bucket, so you can self-host the core URL-to-markdown engine. The image is described as the 'open-source branch', and features such as the residential/datacenter proxy pool are explicitly SaaS-only with a key required, so self-hosted parity with the hosted r.jina.ai service is not established. missing for 10: documented feature parity between the self-hosted branch and the hosted service (e.g. proxy pool, s.jina.ai search, ReaderLM-v2 extraction), detailed deployment/configuration docs, independent hands-on corroboration of a self-hosted deployment.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: A prebuilt image of the open-source branch is published to GitHub Container Registry. It bundles headless Chrome, LibreOffice, and CJK fonts, so you can run Reader without building it yourself.
Point Reader at an S3-compatible bucket to cache fetched pages and reuse them across requests
